findings.title: Noor's line is asked for on a Call that was missed (an answer that ends after the ring-out)
findings.evidence: Commit f0b0043 put the op `line:noor.call.1` on the rituals call_hand_over and call_answer (data/rituals.json:71,73). ItemSim runs a ritual's ops when its gesture completes, without asking again whether the Call still rings (src/core/item_sim.gd:789), and DriveSim._take_the_call then returns because BossSim.answer() refuses (src/core/drive_sim.gd:870). Driven headless (probes/late_window.gd and late_drag.gd under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/subrev/): a hand-over made as fast as the hand goes (0.49 s from press to release) and begun with 0.4 s or less of the 8 s ring left, or a TAP whose release falls after the ring-out (pressed in the last 0.05 s), gives `call_resolved {answered: false}`, then `ritual_completed`, then `line_requested noor.call.1`. In the running drive scene, through the grip action, on Dawn started with DriveSim.begin_boss: the Subtitles layer shows 'Noor: Baba? Are you awake?' while the snapshot says call 'over' and boss.call_answered is false (picture /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/subrev/mine/boss_dawn_late_hand_over.png). The same on a scratch merge with the main line. It goes against GDD 10.4 ('Ignore it: None. The true ending is lost') and against the commit's own sentence 'A Call left to ring out says nothing'; the check only lets the phone ring untouched (tools/subtitles_check_body.gd:724).
findings.fix: Take the two `line:noor.call.1` ops out of data/rituals.json and ask for the line where the answer is known to be taken: one `_emit("line_requested", {"id": "noor.call.1"})` after the `call_resolved` in DriveSim._take_the_call. That is src/core, so it is for the main line, in the merge commit or the one after (the main line already asks for `call.noor.rings` that way). Tried in a scratch copy: both late cases ask for nothing, an answer in time still asks once, and the check passes except its check at tools/subtitles_check_body.gd:714, which must then hold the opposite; add the two late cases to the Call section. Without src/core the same can be done in drive_controller.gd where it forwards a `call_resolved` with answered true.

findings.title: Against the main line as it is now (b26cde6) the merge has one conflict, and check.sh fails until four speaker lines are added
findings.evidence: `git merge-tree --write-tree m10/subtitles-in claude/dazzling-sagan-bi0r2c`: CONFLICT in src/game/game.gd, the line of VALUE_ARGS (this branch appends "say", M8 on the main line appends "ride"); every other file merges by itself. In the unpacked merge with that line resolved, tools/subtitles_check.gd reports 112 checks, 1 failure: 'each of the 13 speakers the line table names has a line of its own; missing: Soldier, Drummer, Student, Boy', so tools/check.sh would print CHECK FAILED. With the eight rows added, tools/check.sh in that scratch merge prints CHECK OK (parse 89 scripts; data 227 lines, 0 errors; tests RESULT: OK in 655 s; subtitles 112 checks, 0 failures; smoke 2 scenes and 12 runs, 0 failures; log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/subrev/check_merged.log). The integration report foresaw the rows; the conflict is new, because the main line has moved on since (the report says 'with the main line no conflict').
findings.fix: In the merge: keep both names in VALUE_ARGS (..., "give", "ride", "say") with this branch's two comment lines about --say; add `speaker.soldier,,Soldier,true`, `speaker.drummer,,Drummer,true`, `speaker.student,,Student,true`, `speaker.boy,,Boy,true` to data/lines_en.csv and the same four ids with empty text (`speaker.soldier,,,true` and so on) to data/lines_ar.csv; then run tools/subtitles_shots.sh and commit the two pictures that change there (call, key).

findings.title: Nothing is ever dropped from the queue: after the merge, passenger chatter makes a tell come seconds late
findings.evidence: SubtitleQueue.push appends without limit (src/view/subtitle_queue.gd:124) and SubtitlesView.say queues every request (src/view/subtitles_view.gd:84), also one for a line that is already showing or waiting. On this base only the Call asks for a line, so it cannot be seen here; on the scratch merge with the main line it can (probes/drummer_taps.gd, probes/chatter_then_ring.gd): with the drummer beside him (--ride=drummer), six TAPs on his shoulder in 1.5 s ask for six lines ('Your tea, driver.' and '(he drums)' three times each) and subtitles run on for 7.67 s after the last TAP. On Dawn's road, two TAPs just before the phone rings put the ring's line '(his phone rings in his pocket: Noor)' on screen 2.56 s after call_started; six TAPs put it there 7.63 s after, of a ring of 8 s. The main line asks for that line as the visual half of a tell (its comment cites GDD 17.2), and GDD 11.3 makes a heckle's subtitle its 2 s tell. The builder listed 'no cap on the queue' and the heckle as matters for M9; with M8's passengers it is there at the merge.
findings.fix: View-side, smallest: in SubtitlesView.say() do not queue a line that is already showing or waiting (let Part carry its line id), and cap what waits at a tuning constant (for example `subtitle_max_waiting`), dropping the oldest waiting request; one check for each. Which lines may be dropped is a decision to record. The full answer needs the simulation (not this branch): a key in the payload of line_requested that marks a tell, so that the view shows it at once.

findings.title: A wrapped right-to-left line that begins with a Latin word runs the wrong way
findings.evidence: The view joins the lines of a part with "\n" (src/view/subtitles_view.gd:142); a Label treats each as a paragraph of its own and takes its direction from its own first strong character. With an Arabic line table made in memory (as the tool's rtl_shot does) and a text of two lines that the queue cuts just before 'I-99', the drive scene draws the second line left to right as a whole: 'I-99' stands at the left end, where an Arabic reader comes to it last (picture /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/subrev/mine/rtl_latin_second_line_crop.png; probe probes/rtl_scene.gd). GDD 16.6: 'so right-to-left text works when Arabic lines arrive'. The builder's picture and probe had Latin words only in the middle of a line.
findings.fix: Join the lines with U+2028 (line separator) instead of "\n" in _show() and split by it in shown_lines(): the Label still breaks the line, and both lines stay one paragraph with one direction. Tried in a scratch copy: 'I-99' is drawn at the right end (picture /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/subrev/mine_fix/rtl_latin_second_line_crop.png) and the check fails only where it compares text.text with "\n".join (tools/subtitles_check_body.gd:586), which changes with it. The first line of a second part of a long text still decides for itself.

findings.title: An exchange is split only while its speaker column says ', then ' in English
findings.evidence: SubtitleQueue.exchange() splits a row only when its speaker column holds ', then ' (src/view/subtitle_queue.gd:24, 68-77), and Lines.get_speaker() gives the Arabic column once a writer fills it. With wreck.children.1 in an Arabic table made in memory, the speaker column written in Arabic ('guest, then Abu Noor') and the text holding its ' / ', the scene shows ONE subtitle: the whole speaker column as the tag and both things said in one line with the ' / ' in it (picture /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/subrev/mine/rtl_exchange_speaker_arabic_crop.png). With the Arabic speaker column left empty the same row is split and each side stands under the Arabic name from its speaker.* line. Nothing tells the writer which to do, and no check holds it (no row of lines_ar.csv names a speaker today).
findings.fix: Smallest: make it the rule that the speaker column of lines_ar.csv stays empty (names are translated in the speaker.* rows): one check in `_speakers()` of tools/subtitles_check_body.gd that no row of lines_ar.csv names a speaker, and a line in DECISIONS.md. Or have say() take who speaks from the English row.

findings.title: Two planted faults pass the check: a tag not taken from the speaker's line, and --say asking for nothing
findings.evidence: Planted in a scratch copy, one at a time, and run through tools/subtitles_check.gd (probes/mut.py, mutants2.py): (a) src/view/subtitles_view.gd:91 with `_queue.push(said[0], said[1])` in place of `Lines.get_speaker_name(said[0])`: 112 checks, 0 failures, because every English speaker line has the text of its column; the decision that tags are lines of their own is held for Lines, not for the view. (b) src/game/drive_controller.gd with the `--say` loop asking for nothing: 112 checks, 0 failures, and the smoke run with --say only looks for error lines. Eleven other faults of mine were caught (no clear on `wreck` or on `arrived`, a setting not applied live, the first frame counted, no queue, the box at the top, the tag hidden, a long text cut off, and others).
findings.fix: Two checks: in `_view()`, with a line table made in memory in which speaker.noor has another text, hold that view.shown_speaker() is that text; in `_in_the_scene()`, start the scene with {"say": SHORT_LINE} and hold that its Subtitles layer shows it.

findings.title: A text shown in parts is held 0.06 s per cut less than the rule asks for the whole; the decision says the opposite
findings.evidence: parts_of() times each part by part.joined().length() (src/view/subtitle_queue.gd:109), so the space at each cut between parts is counted nowhere. subtitle.test.long has 143 characters and asks for 8.58 s by GDD 16.6 ('0.06 s per character'); its two parts (79 and 63 characters) are held 4.74 s + 3.78 s = 8.52 s, and a frame each at most. Of 20,000 random texts of 1 to 40 words, 9,798 were held in all for less than max(1.5, 0.06 x characters), by up to 0.24 s (probes/queue_fuzz.gd; no other rule of the wrapping was broken in that run). The builder's decision says 'a long text is held somewhat longer than the rule applied to the whole', and the check at tools/subtitles_check_body.gd:387 passes only because its 100-character example ends in a part of 16 characters that is lifted to 1.5 s.
findings.fix: Count the swallowed space into the part before it (`duration_of(part.joined().length() + 1)` for every part but the last; line 383 of the check follows), or correct the sentence of the decision before it goes into DECISIONS.md; either way let the check hold the sum for subtitle.test.long.

findings.title: GDD 17.3's font slot per language is not there
findings.evidence: GDD 17.3: 'Use a font slot per language in settings; the owner will add an Arabic font.' The labels take the theme's font (src/view/subtitles_view.gd:145-153), no setting names a font, and the Arabic of artifacts/m10_subtitles_rtl.png is drawn through the engine's fallback to a font of this machine, which an exported game elsewhere may not have. The integration engineer lists it under left_undone; the piece is described as implementing 17.3.
findings.fix: A setting per locale (for example `font_ar`, default "") read in _configure() and on Lines.locale_changed and applied to both labels with add_theme_font_override("font", ...); or leave it to the settings piece of M10 and mark it NEEDS OWNER in PROGRESS.md.

findings.title: The view's file is not the subtitle_view.gd of GDD 13.2
findings.evidence: GDD 13.2 lists `subtitle_view.gd` under src/view, and D-012 reads that list as the required minimum. The piece's file is src/view/subtitles_view.gd (class SubtitlesView); the builder's first decision says so and gives no reason.
findings.fix: Rename the file and its .uid with git mv and follow it in scenes/drive.tscn (the ext_resource path) and in VIEW_SCRIPT of tools/subtitles_check_body.gd; or keep the name and record it in DECISIONS.md.

verdict: On its own base the branch is sound and may be merged, but not by a plain merge, and one behaviour should be put right in the same step. What I ran at 312994b with a clean tree: tools/check.sh prints CHECK OK (parse 84 scripts, data 161 lines and 0 errors, tests RESULT: OK in 355 s, subtitles 112 checks and 0 failures, smoke 2 scenes and 6 runs); the subtitles check also passes three times in real time under load and at 20 frames a second; tools/subtitles_shots.sh retook all fourteen pictures and each is the committed file byte for byte, and I read them. The rules hold: nothing under src/core, tests, docs or wip is touched, the edits to the shared files are small (drive_controller.gd +7, game.gd +8 -2, drive.tscn +4, check.sh +2, smoke_all.gd +2), the view reads no snapshot and changes nothing, numbers are in tuning.json, names and lines go through Lines, and the three commit messages end as required. Tried beyond the reports: the Storm started with begin_boss (the subtitle stands over thick dust, the HUD does not touch it), Dawn started with begin_boss (answered in time her line is shown once and nothing more through the 30 s of talk), a real Wreck in a Telling's scene (three parts showing and waiting are gone in the frame of the `wreck`; the Table's exchange asked for after it runs 0.21 s into the Telling told again, as the builder said), a short line after a long one (the box shrinks), a subtitle at a stop, settings files with wrong types (ignored) and an unknown size (one warning). What must change: (1) in the merge itself, the conflict in game.gd and the eight speaker rows (finding 2), without which check.sh fails; with them the scratch merge with b26cde6 prints CHECK OK. (2) The Call's line (finding 1): it is this branch's data that makes Noor speak on a missed Call, but the right fix is one line in src/core, so it belongs to the main line in the merge commit or the one after. (3) A decision on the queue (finding 3) before M9's heckles, since with M8's passengers a tell can already be late. The low findings can wait. Not findings against this branch, because they need src/core or the owner: line_requested from the simulation when the Call is taken; a key in its payload that marks a tell (and one that ends a line early, for the ring written out); the Wreck's line announced after `wreck`; validator rules for speaker lines and the subtitle constants; a registered test in tests/tests.json (the piece has only its tool, which also holds today's stand-in of D-039, the Telling begun again with the next seed, and will have to follow M9); the builder's and the integrator's decisions written into DECISIONS.md; and for the owner, the subtitle box lying over the horn, the left stalks and the key at the bottom centre, and the Wreck's exchange taking 3.18 s against the 3 s of GDD 3.2. I edited nothing in the repository; my probes, pictures and logs are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/subrev/ (probes/, mine/, mine_fix/, shots/, check.log, check_merged.log).
